span: "In the center of the <term>bhaga</term> <gloss>source of phenomena/womb</gloss> is the space, adorned with five spaces; possessing a navel and filaments, it is beautiful with eight petals." Thus it appears. Regarding "indestructible," this is because it is the essence of the **Dharma Body**. "All empowerments" refers to the master, the secret, and the wisdom empowerments. The "empowerment of those" refers to the wisdom-gnosis, which is characterized by the phrase "the fourth is likewise." Because he is the essence of that, **Vajradhara** is called "the empowerment of all." All the families divided by the inclinations of sentient beings are the hundred, the five, or the three families. As it is said: "The families are explained as being of a hundred types; condensed, they are of five types; through the division of body, speech, and mind, they later become three types." The **Blessed One**, who is the nature of those, is so because he emanates them. Therefore, the word "knowing" means "emanating." "Indivisible speech" refers to speech characterized by union with a <term>mudrā</term> <gloss>consort/seal</gloss>. "Explained without intention" means showing reality very clearly. "Conduct without proliferation" is the nature of entering into union with a <term>mudrā</term> through the gateway of all such conduct. From the phrase "the outcaste woman" down to "because it is the yoga of conceptualization," it refers to the practitioners of **Akṣobhya**, **Vairocana**, and **Amitābha** in due order. In a place secluded from people, smeared with cow dung and the like, one should draw a wheel of the nature of the support and the supported, or meditate on it with the mind. In its center, one places a well-trained, beautiful, and well-adorned girl of one's own family: an outcaste, a laundry-maid, or a dancer, aged twelve, twenty, or sixteen. They are associated with the blue, red, or white water-lily <note>original: "utpala"</note>, and are pervaded by the five families. Having placed them and preceded by passion and offerings, one should dwell having performed the application <note>of the rites</note> through the stage of withdrawal.
old_translation:
"In the center of the womb <term>bhaga</term> is space,
Adorned by the five spaces;
With a center and filaments,
It is beautiful with eight petals."

So it appears. Regarding "indestructible," this is because it is the essence of the Truth Body <term>Dharmakāya</term>. Regarding "all empowerments," these are called the Master, the Secret, and the Wisdom. Regarding "the empowerment of those as well," this is the Wisdom-Knowledge <note>the third empowerment</note>. The phrase "the fourth is likewise" describes its characteristic. Because he is the essence of that, **Vajradhara** is called "the one of all empowerments." 

According to the divisions of the intentions of sentient beings, all families are either a hundred, or five, or three. As it is said:
"The families are explained as being a hundred;
When condensed, they are of five types;
By the division of body, speech, and mind,
They further become three types."

The **Blessed One**, who is the essence of those, is so called because he emanates them. Therefore, the word "knowing" <note>in the text</note> has the meaning of "emanating." "Indivisible speech" refers to speech characterized by entering into union with the consort <term>mudrā</term>. "Explained without intentional meaning" refers to the teaching of reality with extreme clarity. "Conduct without elaboration" is characterized by entering into union with the consort through the gateway of whatever conduct is necessary. 

From the phrase "the outcaste woman" <term>pukkasī</term> down to "because it is the yoga of conceptualization," the text describes how yogis of the **Akṣobhya**, **Vairocana**, and **Amitābha** families should go to a place secluded from people, smeared with cow dung and so forth. There, they should either draw a mandala of the "supported and the supporter" <note>the palace and the deities</note> or meditate on it with the mind. In the center, they should place a woman who is well-trained, of good form, well-adorned, and compatible with their own family—such as an outcaste woman, a laundryman's daughter, or a dancer's daughter, aged twelve, twenty, or sixteen. She should be like a blue, red, or white lotus. Having established her as pervaded by the five families, and having preceded with passion and offerings, one should abide while performing the "near-usage" <note>sexual union</note> through the sequence of "individual withdrawal" <term>pratyāhāra</term>.
